title: Review (Weak): on fresh seed 12 the ring's effect on division replicates (16 vs 10 persistent splits) but the ring-free Df=0.3 twin does not match the ringed world (10 splits, like the ablation)
summary: I re-ran c15's nematic fuel-cell world on seed 12 with labkit in three arms: the ringed world, the ring ablation (chis=0) and c20's matched ring-free twin (chis=0, Df=0.3). Persistent splits / max generation / final bodies: world 16 / 3 / 23, chis=0 10 / 2 / 20, slow-D 10 / 3 / 20. Core fuel: 0.56 (world), 0.35 (chis=0), 0.77 (slow-D); the ring is membrane-like in 85/85 world bodies and 0 in both ring-free arms. Shapes look alike in all three (compare_s12.png). So the ring raises division over its ablation on this seed as on seed 11, but uniformly slower fuel diffusion does not reproduce that gain here although it holds even more core fuel.

observations.W: rerun/*_s12/FACTS.md: persistent splits world 16, chis=0 10, slow-D(Df 0.3) 10; core fuel 0.56 / 0.35 / 0.77 (ringstat_s12.txt): the slow-D twin keeps more fuel but does not divide like the ringed world

seeds_run.result: fail for the finding's equivalence: slow-D twin 10 splits vs world 16 (ablation 10); the ring-vs-ablation difference replicates

controls_run.W: rerun/chis0_s12 (ring ablation) and rerun/slowD_s12 (ring-free twin with Df=0.3), same seed, grid and duration

verdicts.limitation: Split counts are small (10-16) and one seed each; across the two seeds now known the slow-D twin matches the world on seed 11 (15 vs 15) and the ablation on seed 12 (10 vs 10), so the equivalence is not established either way. More seeds, or a dose series in Df, would decide it. Not tested: Df=0.03, other seeds, dt/2.
